text:
Marta R.: heads up — noticed a spike in 5xx+ latency and users jumping between canary and stable during the 09:10 deploy window. lots of session bounce for the same user ids
David K.: can you paste a sample request id or cookie header so I can trace?
Marta R.: sample: request_id=abcd-1234, cookie=redwood_sid=eyJhbGci..., x-client-region=us-west-2
Ashley P.: any rate-limit or quota events around that time? sounds like fallback routing when canary is 'full'
CI-Bot: deploy-redwood/canary-2026-03-09 finished: success
Marta R.: CI-Bot shows success but we see ~3% of sessions get served by stable model after initially hitting canary; users report changed completions mid-conversation (bad UX)
David K.: I'm running a quick query on router logs for split decisions. give me a minute
Liam S.: note: routing policy for this rollout uses cookie-consistent hashing then header-based override if present. We recently added a tiny-weights optimization (weights < 0.5% treated as prob=0) — could that be clamping?
David K.: found a pattern: these requests have a missing cookie on some subsequent calls (mobile background refresh) so we treat them as new sessions. But even when cookie present, hash_bucket changed between calls: shows different bucket values for same session id
Ashley P.: code snippet from router (simplified):
```
bucket = murmur32(hash_key) % total_buckets
if bucket < canary_threshold_buckets:
  route = CANARY
else:
  route = STABLE
```
David K.: murmur32 returns unsigned int. on js layer `total_buckets` is a float for low-weight split (e.g., 0.01 * 10000 = 100). but if total_buckets gets coerced to 0 in some paths it triggers `mod 0` fallback which picks default route 
Marta R.: mod 0? that explains instant fallback to stable for some requests. any idea which path sets total_buckets=0?
David K.: saw it in the batch-aggregation path where we compute `effective_buckets = Math.floor(weight * BUCKET_SCALE)` but we early-return for very small floats and set effective_buckets=0. then `total_buckets = effective_buckets` gets passed to downstream router without guard
Liam S.: bug: router should never call `%` with 0. fix: clamp minimum to 1 and prefer probabilistic check for tiny weights rather than zeroing out. Also add telemetry metric `split_mod_zero_count`
Ashley P.: agreed. quick patch: ensure `effective_buckets = Math.max(1, Math.floor(...))` and add assertion in router: `if (total_buckets === 0) { log.error(...); total_buckets = 1 }`
Marta R.: can we hotfix this on stable and canary? the deploy window is still open but we should avoid rolling forward until patch lands
CI-Bot: PR opened by david-k: https://git.redwood/internal/pr/4821 - "guard mod-by-zero in routing buckets"
David K.: running canary of the fix to 2% now. monitoring tracked sessions: previously bounced users reduced to near 0.2%
Ashley P.: also propose changing precedence: header overrides should only apply if header is explicitly set by trusted infra (not client-set). we found some mobile SDKs setting `x-canary-prefer` for sampling purposes which interferes
Liam S.: good call — add `header_trusted_sources` whitelist and log `header_override_untrusted` when triggered
Marta R.: action items: 1) merge PR 4821 (done if tests pass), 2) add telemetry counters and dashboard tile showing `split_mismatch_rate` by client platform, 3) update rollout docs to warn about small-weight optimizations. I'll create the ticket
David K.: ticket created: INC-3257 — notes + reproduction steps + raw logs attached
Marta R.: thanks everyone. I'll keep the canary paused until tomorrow's safety window to be safe :thumbsup:
Ashley P.: marking follow-up: do an audit of all active rollouts for weights < 1% and ensure they use probabilistic sampling instead of bucket-flooring
CI-Bot: ticket INC-3257 updated, and PR 4821 merged to main in 10m
Marta R.: closing loop here — we restored stable behavior, documented the fix. ping me if you see regressions
